text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prince Hassan calls for Western approach (to region) based on dialogue not oil. "It is unfair to ask us to commit economic suicide because we are neighbours of besieged Iraq. The policy of dual containment is a failure."
- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti praises outcome of Algerian reconciliation conference.
- Planning Minister Rima Khalaf says central bank reserves have reached safe level; we do not intend to devalue the dinar and we are looking at best ways to achieve privatisation.
- Lower House of Parliament Speaker Saed Hayel Srour says dissolving chamber and holding early elections is one of King Hussein's rights.
- Islamic Action Front deputies say they will not take part in government. Srour says there is no reason for calling early elections.
- Jordan Central Bank puts in circulation new 10 dinar banknotes.
- Transport Minister Nasser al-Lawzi says studies under way for privatising public transport company and Aqaba railway corporation.
- Prince Hassan says current situation critical, Iraq's situation is sounding alarm bells.
- Labour minister says Saudi Arabia has employed 2,000 female Jordanian teachers.
- Jordan pledges continued support for activities of the International Committee of the Red Cross.
- Foreign exchange reserves will be up by $250 million by end of 1996.
- Number of corruption, bribery cases sent to court rises to 101.
